stories.headline: Trump Extends Iran Ceasefire Indefinitely but Maintains Naval Blockade as Talks Stall

key_facts.fact: Trump announced on Truth Social he would extend the ceasefire indefinitely at Pakistan's request, saying Iran's government is 'seriously fractured' and directing the military to 'continue the Blockade'
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said he would extend the U.S. ceasefire with Iran until Tehran provides a unified proposal, but added that the U.S. military blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would remain in place.

key_facts.fact: Iran refused to attend Round 2 talks in Islamabad, citing US 'excessive demands, unrealistic expectations, constant shifts in stance, repeated contradictions, and the ongoing naval blockade'
key_facts.excerpt: CNN reported that top officials believe there was little point in Vance traveling to Pakistan for the talks. They believe Iran didn't reply to US proposals because its leaders don't yet have consensus.

key_facts.fact: Vice President Vance's planned trip to Pakistan was canceled; a White House official confirmed the delegation would not travel on Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. delegation's trip to Pakistan, where Vice President Vance and other officials were planning to discuss the ceasefire with Iranian counterparts, will not happen on Tuesday, a White House official confirmed.

key_facts.fact: Iran's parliamentary adviser Mahdi Mohammadi dismissed the ceasefire extension as 'meaningless,' warning that 'continuing the siege is no different from bombing and must be responded to militarily'
key_facts.excerpt: Mahdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran's parliament speaker, said the move 'means nothing' and argued that the 'losing side cannot set the terms'.

key_facts.fact: A Pentagon intelligence assessment found Iran retains its 'key military capabilities,' contradicting Trump and Defense Secretary Hegseth's claims that Iran's forces suffered irreversible damage
key_facts.excerpt: The intelligence assessment instead indicates that Iran remains a 'potent regional power,' casting doubt on claims that its 'air force has been destroyed' and its 'navy decimated'.

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed; the US has imposed a naval blockade turning back 27 vessels, boarding one commercial ship, and seizing a sanctioned oil tanker
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. has also recently imposed a naval blockade on Iranian commercial and oil ships in the Strait, turning back 27 vessels, boarding one commercial ship, and seizing a sanctioned oil tanker.

stories.headline: CSIS: US Burned Through ~50% of Key Missile Stockpiles in 39-Day Iran Air Campaign

key_facts.fact: The US expended at least 45% of its Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) stockpile, at least 50% of THAAD interceptors, and nearly 50% of Patriot air defense interceptors in 39 days of the Iran air campaign
key_facts.excerpt: In the 39 days of the air and missile campaign before the ceasefire, U.S. forces heavily used the seven munitions. For four of them, the United States may have expended more than half of the prewar inventory.

key_facts.fact: Approximately 30% of the Navy's Tomahawk cruise missile inventory was expended, along with over 20% of long-range JASSM stockpiles and ~20% of SM-3 and SM-6 naval interceptors
key_facts.excerpt: The US military has also expended approximately 30% of its Tomahawk missile stockpile; more than 20% of its stockpile of long-range Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles; and approximately 20% of its SM-3 and SM-6 missiles.

key_facts.fact: CSIS concluded that high munitions expenditures created a 'window of increased vulnerability in the western Pacific,' with stockpiles now insufficient to confront a near-peer adversary like China
key_facts.excerpt: The risk—which will persist for many years—lies in future wars. Even before the Iran war, stockpiles were deemed insufficient for a peer competitor fight. That shortfall is now even more acute.

key_facts.fact: Replenishing stockpiles to prewar levels will take 1-4 years; expanding to levels adequate for a China conflict will take additional years beyond that, even with new Pentagon procurement contracts
key_facts.excerpt: It will take one to four years to replenish these inventories and several years after that to expand them to where they need to be.

key_facts.fact: Diminished inventories will also affect US supply of Patriot, THAAD, and PrSM to Ukraine and other allies, as the US competes with partner nations seeking to replenish and expand their own stockpiles
key_facts.excerpt: Diminished inventories will also affect the U.S. supply of Patriot, THAADs, and PrSMs to Ukraine and other allies and partners. The United States will compete with those countries that also want to replenish and expand inventories.

key_facts.fact: Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the military 'has everything it needs to execute' presidential directives across all combatant commands
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said that the military 'has everything it needs to execute' presidential directives, citing successful recent operations.

US at risk of running out of missiles if another war breaks out after depleting stockpile in Iran operations

stories.headline: Pentagon Unveils Record $1.5T Budget With $70B+ for Drones, Largest-Ever Drone Investment

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon's FY2027 budget requests $1.5 trillion total — $1.15 trillion through appropriations and $350 billion via reconciliation, a 22.6% increase overall
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon asks Congress to approve $1.5 trillion in total funding — $1.15 trillion through its yearly appropriations process, and $350 billion via the legislative tactic of reconciliation.

key_facts.fact: The budget allocates $53.6 billion for autonomy, drone platforms and contested logistics, plus $21 billion for munitions, counter-drone tech and collaborative combat aircraft — totaling $70B+
key_facts.excerpt: Requesting $53.6 billion for autonomy, drone platforms and contested logistics, along with $21 billion for munitions, counter-drone technologies and advanced systems like the collaborative combat aircraft.

key_facts.fact: FY2026 comparison: Pentagon sought only $13.4B for autonomous systems and $3.1B for counter-drone, making FY2027 a roughly 4x increase in drone/counter-drone spending
key_facts.excerpt: In comparison, Pentagon officials sought $13.4 billion for autonomous systems and $3.1 billion for counter-drone capabilities in fiscal year 2026.

key_facts.fact: The Defense Autonomous Warfare Group (DAWG) received a 24,000%+ funding boost — from $225.9 million in FY2026 to up to $54.6 billion requested in FY2027
key_facts.excerpt: A colossal, more than 24,000% boost for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group (DAWG) — from $225.9 million received in fiscal 2026 to up to $54.6 billion requested in fiscal 2027.

key_facts.fact: The budget also includes a 'presidential priorities category' for Golden Dome missile defense, the Drone Dominance Program, AI/data infrastructure, and the defense industrial base
key_facts.excerpt: The budget request also includes a 'presidential priorities category' for investments in Golden Dome, the Drone Dominance Program, artificial intelligence and data infrastructure.

sources.title: DOD moves to make its largest-ever investment in drones and anti-drone weapons
Pentagon details record $1.5 trillion defense budget request

stories.headline: UK Inflation Jumps to 3.3% in March as Iran War Drives Largest Fuel Price Spike in 3 Years

key_facts.fact: UK CPI rose to 3.3% annually in March from 3% in February, in line with economist expectations and the first official data showing the Iran war's impact on UK consumer prices
key_facts.excerpt: The annual consumer price inflation rate increased to a three-month high of 3.3%, from 3% the previous month. The rise was 'largely due to increased fuel prices'.

key_facts.fact: Motor fuel prices rose 8.7% month-on-month, the largest increase since June 2022 (shortly after Russia's Ukraine invasion); petrol hit 140.2p/litre, diesel jumped 17.6p to 158.7p
key_facts.excerpt: The rise was 'largely due to increased fuel prices', while air fares also contributed. ONS Chief Economist Grant Fitzner said fuel prices saw 'their largest increase for over three years'.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices are up ~30% since the conflict began on February 28 and have been trading around $100/barrel for several weeks
key_facts.excerpt: As a net importer of energy, the U.K. is particularly vulnerable to global energy price shocks like the one caused by conflict in the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: Economists warn inflation could rise further to 4%+ later this year; the IMF has warned the UK faces the hardest hit of the G7 from the Iran war
key_facts.excerpt: Inflation is set to rise further in coming months, possibly to 4%, as higher energy prices impact household bills.

key_facts.fact: Bank of England expected to hold rates at 3.75% at its April 30 meeting; a majority of economists polled by Reuters expect rates unchanged for the rest of 2026
key_facts.excerpt: A majority of economists polled by Reuters expect the BOE to keep rates unchanged for the rest of the year, arguing policymakers will choose to 'look through' the spike in inflation caused by external factors.

key_facts.fact: Services inflation also rose to 4.5% from 4.3%, and food prices increased 3.7% annually; core inflation (ex food/energy) edged down to 3.1% from 3.2%
key_facts.excerpt: Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, actually dropped to 3.1 per cent in March from 3.2 per cent. Services inflation increased to 4.5 per cent from 4.3 per cent.

stories.headline: Roche's Fenebrutinib Halves MS Relapses in Phase III, Potential First BTK Inhibitor for MS

key_facts.fact: Phase III FENhance 1 showed 51.1% reduction in annualized relapse rate (p<0.001) and FENhance 2 showed 58.5% reduction (p<0.0001) vs. teriflunomide in relapsing MS over 96 weeks
key_facts.excerpt: Fenebrutinib reduced the annualized relapse rate (ARR) by 51.1% (p<0.001) in FENhance 1 and 58.5% (p<0.0001) in FENhance 2 compared with teriflunomide over 96 weeks.

key_facts.fact: The reduction equates to patients having approximately one relapse every 17 years — more than double the relapse-free interval seen with teriflunomide
key_facts.excerpt: This equates to patients having approximately one relapse every 17 years, more than half the relapses seen with teriflunomide.

key_facts.fact: Fenebrutinib could become the first-in-class BTK inhibitor and the first high-efficacy oral therapy for both relapsing MS and primary progressive MS (PPMS)
key_facts.excerpt: Fenebrutinib could become a first-in-class BTK inhibitor and the first and only high-efficacy oral for both RMS and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS).

key_facts.fact: Previously, the Phase III FENtrepid study in PPMS also met its primary endpoint; combined data from all three pivotal studies will be submitted to regulatory authorities
key_facts.excerpt: The collective positive results across all three pivotal studies demonstrate that fenebrutinib consistently showed a profound benefit on relapsing and progressive disease biology.

key_facts.fact: Results were presented as a late-breaking presentation at the 2026 American Academy of Neurology Annual Meeting in Chicago; 1,497 total patients enrolled across both studies
key_facts.excerpt: The results were shared today as a late-breaking presentation at the 2026 American Academy of Neurology (AAN) Annual Meeting in Chicago.

sources.title: Genentech's Fenebrutinib Significantly Reduced Relapses Versus Standard of Care to Approximately One Every 17 Years in RMS

stories.headline: FDA Approves Sanofi's Tzield for Children as Young as 1 to Delay Type 1 Diabetes Onset

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Sanofi's Tzield (teplizumab-mzwv) to expand its indication from 8 years and older to children as young as 1 year to delay stage 3 type 1 diabetes in patients with stage 2 T1D
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA has approved the supplemental biologic license application for Tzield, expanding the indication from eight years and older to as young as one year of age to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes.

key_facts.fact: Tzield is the first disease-modifying therapy approved for children under 8 diagnosed with stage 2 T1D; it is a CD3-directed monoclonal antibody administered as a 14-day IV infusion
key_facts.excerpt: Tzield is the first disease-modifying therapy for children aged one year and above diagnosed with stage 2 T1D.

key_facts.fact: Approval granted under priority review based on the PETITE-T1D phase 4 study, which enrolled 23 participants under 8 years evaluating safety and pharmacokinetics
key_facts.excerpt: The approval was granted under a priority review process and is supported by one-year data from the PETITE-T1D phase 4 study, evaluating safety and pharmacokinetics in young children.

key_facts.fact: Tzield is also under FDA review for a potential indication to delay stage 3 T1D progression in patients 8+ years recently diagnosed with stage 3 disease
key_facts.excerpt: Tzield is also under FDA review for a potential indication to delay the progression of stage 3 T1D in patients aged eight years and older who have been recently diagnosed with stage 3 disease.

key_facts.fact: Already approved in the EU, UK, China, Canada, Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, and Brazil for patients 8+ with stage 2 T1D; first approved in the US in November 2022
key_facts.excerpt: Tzield is approved in the EU (under the name Teizeild), in the UK, China, Canada, Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, and Brazil to delay the onset of stage 3 T1D.

sources.title: Sanofi's Tzield approved in the US to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes in young children

stories.headline: Xi Jinping Calls for Strait of Hormuz Reopening in First Such Demand, During Call With Saudi Crown Prince

key_facts.fact: Xi called for an 'immediate and comprehensive ceasefire' in the Middle East and said that normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz 'serves the common interest of regional countries and the international community'
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese president called for an immediate and comprehensive ceasefire and cessation of hostilities in the Middle East, while saying that normal passage through the Strait of Hormuz 'serves the common interest'.

key_facts.fact: The comments, made Monday in a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, mark the first time Xi has publicly called for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, per China's Xinhua news agency
key_facts.excerpt: Xi's comments on Monday in a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman were the first time he mentioned reopening the Strait of Hormuz, according to China's state-run media site Xinhua.

key_facts.fact: China's close relationship with Iran and reliance on oil trade have suffered during the Strait's effective closure; Beijing is also balancing ties with Gulf countries Iran has attacked
key_facts.excerpt: China's close relationship with Iran and reliance on oil trade have suffered during the Strait's effective closure. Meanwhile, China is balancing its ties with Gulf countries that Iran has attacked.

key_facts.fact: Xi met with UAE President Sheikh Khaled last week, emphasizing 'sustainable security architecture' in the region and preventing the world 'from returning to the law of the jungle'
key_facts.excerpt: Xi met with UAE President Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan last week, emphasizing the importance of 'sustainable security architecture' in the region.

key_facts.fact: Singapore FM Balakrishnan warned that the Strait of Hormuz crisis is 'just a dry run' for what could happen in the Pacific if the US and China clash, calling chokepoints a critical strategic factor
key_facts.excerpt: Should a war break out between China and the U.S. in the Pacific, 'what you are seeing in the Strait of Hormuz will be a dry run,' Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan said.
